messages:
Priya: Bringing sakura-v1 through compact-int4 onboarding. Smoke shows a reproducible invisible-char insertion between kanji and inline furigana when Arabic diacritics appear later in the same sentence. FP16 fine, int4 has an extra NBSP or ZWNJ in different samples. BLEU drops ~6 on ja-zh-srt subset. Anyone seen script-adjacent invisible tokens tied to quant tables? :eyes:

Ken: Can you paste a minimal repro and the quant args? Also state whether this is before or after detok.

Priya: Repro run:```\n./onboard_eval --model sakura-v1 --quant int4 --calib per_channel --quant-hash=fnv --dataset srt-multilang --langs ja,ar,zh --detok unicode --batch 10\n```

Priya: Example (simplified):
FP16 detok: "\u7ae0\u30d5\u30ea\u30ac\u30ca \u0627\u0644\u0633\u0627" (kanji+furigana then Arabic)
int4 detok: "\u7ae0\u00A0\u30d5\u30ea\u30ac\u30ca \u0627\u0644\u0633\u0627" (NBSP inserted between kanji and furigana).
Also saw a variant: "\u7ae0\u200c\u30d5\u30ea\u30ac\u30ca" (ZWNJ) depending on seed.

Hao: Dump the tokenizer token ids + raw bytes for that sample (hex). I'll grep tokenmap for 0xA0 and 0x200C entries.

Priya: Dump:```\n# fp16 token stream ids: [0x5f20, 0x30d5, 0x30ea, 0x30ac, 0x30ca, 0x20, 0x0627...]\n# int4 token stream ids: [0x5f20, 0x00A0, 0x30d5, 0x30ea, 0x30ac, 0x30ca, 0x20, 0x0627...]\n# raw bytes show 0xC2 0xA0 inserted between E4 B8 B0 and E3 83 95 when Arabic combining marks appear later in sentence\n```

QA-bot: Quick eval snapshot (ja-zh-srt subset):
fp16 BLEU: 40.5 chrF:0.605
int4 BLEU: 34.3 chrF:0.562
delta BLEU: -6.2

Ken: Two likely classes: normalization pipeline differs for quantized tokenizer artifacts, or quant table assignment/hash collisions cause a formerly-unused index to map to NBSP/ZWNJ glyph during detok. Have we changed rounding (symmetric->asymmetric) or bucket clipping for int4?

Priya: Quant flags for this run: `--quant-round=asymmetric --quant-clip=0.01 --quant-sparsity=0.1`. I will re-run with symmetric rounding and sparsity=0 to see.

Hao: Also try regenerating the table with a different hash (xxh3) or set `--quant-salt=42`. If the invisible char flips with hash/salt, it's an assignment collision.

Priya: Quick tests: symmetric rounding + sparsity=0 improves BLEU by ~1.5 but NBSP still shows in a subset. Changing hash to xxh3 + salt=42 on a single worker removed the NBSP in all sampled failing lines. Re-running full suite now.

Ken: Sounds like a hash collision in the compaction stage. Please attach the `tokenmap_int4.json` from the failing run to the bug. We should also add a small mixed-script test (kanji+furigana + Arabic diacritics) to the pre-quant smoke harness to catch regressions.

Priya: Filed ML-3078 with repro, attached tokenmap and sample lines. I've added a quick unit to the smoke harness covering 12 mixed-script permutations. Also gated int4 auto-promote for sakura-v1 until the regenerated table lands.

ci-bot: CI: kicked off grid jobs for `quant-hash=[fnv,xxh3]` x `quant-salt=[0,42,99]` x `quant-round=[symmetric,asymmetric]` (6 jobs). Notifying #eng-ml.

Hao: If xxh3+salt fixes consistently, we should switch default compaction hash and record a migration note. For the short term, regenerate tables for sakura-v1 and lark-v2 with the safer hash and re-run onboarding.

Priya: Agreed. I'll coordinate the regen and follow up with results. Thanks all :heart:
